=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:136, 141 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The comment references the obsolete pattern `\[E2E Smoke Test\b` while the implementation uses `^\[E2E `.
  WHY: The comment does not fail at runtime but misleads maintainers about the enforced detector; severity disagreement exists, with the other reviewers classifying it as NIT and x-ai_grok-4_20 classifying it as MAJOR.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:~510-512, 517 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The parent-tracking `gh api` lookup has no wall-clock timeout or bounded wrapper.
  WHY: A slow or hung GitHub API connection can stall the plan step until the job-level timeout instead of reaching the intended fail-open path.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2589-2599 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The PR title/body smoke check uses the unanchored pattern `grep -qiE '\[E2E '`, which can classify production PRs that merely mention an E2E fixture tag mid-string as smoke PRs.
  WHY: Such PRs can enter smoke-specific alert suppression and canary-edit paths; one reviewer noted this is an explicitly accepted tradeoff in the PR description.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:502-517 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The parent-tracking fallback uses raw `gh api` and `jq` instead of the repository's established `_safe_gh_jq` convention.
  WHY: The lookup currently works, but divergent authentication, retry, and rate-limit handling can create inconsistent reliability guarantees; z-ai_glm-5_2 disputed this as a defect because the path deliberately mirrors an incumbent raw-API convention.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:506 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Smoke-detection fallback depends on the issue-body format `Tracking issue: #N`.
  WHY: If the upstream body format changes, `SMOKE_TRACKING_NUM` remains empty and orchestrator-child smoke plans can fail to be detected; z-ai_glm-5_2 disputed this as an established repository convention rather than an undocumented format.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The contract test now pins the detection half of the chain" and "Behaviour matrix against the extracted `plan.yml` step with a stubbed gh, all 6 as designed"
  expected_change_site: tests/test_smoke_alert_silencing_contract.py::test_plan_falls_back_to_orchestrator_parent_title (around lines 237-266) and any sibling test that asserts the runtime outcome of the parent-fallback path
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The test only asserts structural substrings inside the extracted workflow block and does not execute a stubbed `gh api` path to verify that matching parent titles export `ALERT_MSG_LEVEL=SILENT` and `MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT=low`, unreachable parents fail open, and production issues remain unsilenced.
- requirement: "Pin the cross-file contract between plan.yml and orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml"
  expected_change_site: tests/test_smoke_alert_silencing_contract.py::test_plan_falls_back_to_orchestrator_parent_title around the second assert for the orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml pattern
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The test pins that `^\[Orchestrator\] E2E ` exists in both files but does not pin that both regexes accept and reject the same titles; z-ai_glm-5_2 disputed this gap because byte-identical regex literals accept and reject identical inputs by construction.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:136 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Stale comment text `same \`\\[E2E Smoke Test\\b\` pattern` describes the old pattern. The line 141 code now uses `'^\[E2E '`. The comment was not updated when the pattern changed.
  WHY: Does not fail at runtime — it is a documentation stale-pointer that misleads future maintainers about the active pattern.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:~510-512 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new parent-tracking issue lookup invokes `gh api` without a timeout.
  WHY: A slow or unresponsive GitHub API can stall the plan step for the duration of the entire job, blocking the workflow instead of failing open within a bounded interval.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2589-2598 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The PR title/body smoke check uses the unanchored pattern `grep -qiE '\[E2E '`, which can classify production PRs that merely mention an E2E fixture tag mid-string as smoke PRs.
  WHY: Such PRs enter smoke-specific alert suppression and canary-edit paths, suppressing legitimate alerts and potentially incorrectly modifying or referencing the canary test file.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:506 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The smoke-detection fallback depends on an undocumented and brittle issue-body format (`Tracking issue: #N`).
  WHY: If the upstream body format changes, `SMOKE_TRACKING_NUM` remains empty, and orchestrator-child smoke plans will silently fail to be detected, leading to unsuppressed per-phase Telegram alerts on release runs.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:136 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The comment references the obsolete pattern `\[E2E Smoke Test\b` while the implementation now uses `^\[E2E `.
  WHY: No runtime failure; however, stale documentation misleads future maintenance about which patterns are enforced by the precheck, increasing the risk of re-introducing the alert-leak bug.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:502-517 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The parent-tracking fallback uses raw `gh api` and `jq` instead of the repository's established `_safe_gh_jq` helper convention.
  WHY: The lookup works currently, but divergent authentication, retry, and rate-limit handling across equivalent issue lookup paths increases maintenance risk and creates inconsistent reliability guarantees for the orchestrator-managed smoke-plan detection.
- tests/test_smoke_alert_silencing_contract.py::test_plan_falls_back_to_orchestrator_parent_title around lines 244-263 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The contract test only asserts structural substrings and does not execute a stubbed `gh api` path.
  WHY: It does not verify that `ALERT_MSG_LEVEL=SILENT` and `MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT=low` are correctly exported in the plan workflow's job environment.
- tests/test_smoke_alert_silencing_contract.py::test_plan_falls_back_to_orchestrator_parent_title around the second assert for the orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml pattern | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The test does not pin that both cross-file regexes accept and reject the same titles.
  WHY: A future change to one regex could break the cross-file contract while the literal substring assertion still passes.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:136 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The precheck's stale comment still documents the obsolete pattern: `# threshold exported here (same \`\\[E2E Smoke Test\\b\` pattern; the` while the actual grep on line 141 now uses `^\[E2E `.
  WHY: No runtime failure, but future maintainers may believe the detector is still `\[E2E Smoke Test\b` and re-narrow the grep without realising it would break the negative-test and alt-model fixture coverage.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:517 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The new `gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/issues/${SMOKE_TRACKING_NUM}" 2>/dev/null` call has no wall-clock bound.
  WHY: A hung TCP connect can stall the step until the 30-minute job timeout; replacing it with `gh_retry _safe_gh_jq ...` would match the rest of the repository's convention.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2598-2599 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The PR title/body check uses the unanchored pattern `grep -qiE '\[E2E '`.
  WHY: A production PR mentioning an E2E fixture tag can be misclassified, causing smoke-specific alert suppression and a canary-file directive; this was explicitly acknowledged as a deferred tradeoff in the PR description.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:502-517 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The new parent lookup uses raw `gh api` and `jq` rather than `_safe_gh_jq` plus `gh_retry`.
  WHY: Divergent retry and timeout behavior creates inconsistent reliability guarantees.
- tests/test_smoke_alert_silencing_contract.py::test_plan_falls_back_to_orchestrator_parent_title (lines 237-266) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new test only asserts structural substrings and never executes the extracted step body against a stubbed `gh api`.
  WHY: A broken fallback could pass while silently disabling smoke suppression; the advertised six-case behavior matrix is not pinned in CI.
- tests/test_smoke_alert_silencing_contract.py::test_plan_falls_back_to_orchestrator_parent_title second `assert` against `orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The test asserts the literal `^\[Orchestrator\] E2E ` in both files but does not test semantic equivalence against a corpus of titles.
  WHY: Case-sensitivity or other semantic drift could let the files diverge while the substring assertion still passes.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:514 | confidence=unspecified
  PROBLEM: The `Tracking issue: #` parser may produce multiple references; `head -n1` is redundant without a defensive guard.
  WHY: A body containing multiple tracking references could make the parsed parent selection ambiguous.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
